important_semantics: update_reservation_flights preserves the stored price for an unchanged segment and uses current price for a new segment.
update_reservation_flights replaces the complete reservation flight list supplied by the caller.
A successful flight update returns the committed reservation immediately.
The same reservation can be updated again; native Airline has no one-change commitment boundary.
Certificate redemption removes the certificate, but the completed v3 Pilot showed a visible resource-dominance shortcut.
modify_pending_order_items changes status to pending (item modified).
A later item modification on the same order fails while the first write remains committed.
The one-shot batching requirement is explicitly visible in the native Retail policy and tool description.
Gift-card cancellation refunds are immediate and can affect later actions, but this dependency already appears in Benchmark v2.

native_probes.observation: HAT287 was changed to HAT064 and then successfully changed back to HAT287 on the same reservation.
native_probes.implication: A wrong native flight choice is recoverable; a delayed-failure Pilot needs an explicit v3-only commitment boundary.

native_probes.observation: The first item modification committed and changed status; the second call failed with Non-pending order cannot be modified.
native_probes.implication: The native state machine supplies irreversibility, but not hidden knowledge because the batching rule is already explicit.

native_probes.observation: A process-local v3 AirlineTools subclass was registered as a separate domain with 14 tools while the native airline registration continued to construct AirlineTools.
native_probes.implication: A v3-only environment can be wired without editing native domain source or Benchmark v2.

extension_candidates.name: CHANNEL_CONDITIONED_SETTLEMENT_COMMIT
extension_candidates.native_anchor: Historical prices are stored per reserved segment and native updates already compute a historical/current settlement delta.
extension_candidates.required_extension: Expose a stable ticketing channel or settlement-contract field, implement two channel-conditioned settlement baselines, and enforce an explicit one-change commitment budget.
extension_candidates.latent_mapping: Observable contract/channel plus itinerary state determines which settlement baseline must be used before choosing a conditional itinerary branch.
extension_candidates.wrong_action_consequence: The wrong itinerary mutation succeeds, consumes the one allowed change, and leaves a final state that violates the user's conditional goal.
extension_candidates.ordinary_retry: Blocked by the explicit consumed change budget.
extension_candidates.experience_identifiability: Requires paired channel conditions with wrong-branch failure and correct-branch success, including reverse-direction price cases.
extension_candidates.overlap: Builds on v2 P2/P5 but adds an explicit stable selector and commitment consequence; must be described as a clean v3 extension, not a new native tau2 fact.

extension_candidates.name: CHANNEL_CONDITIONED_MODIFICATION_PATH
extension_candidates.native_anchor: Direct update and cancellation/new-booking paths already exist and produce different reservation and payment histories.
extension_candidates.required_extension: Add a visible booking-channel field whose hidden operational contract determines whether benefits and settlement survive direct modification or replacement booking.
extension_candidates.latent_mapping: Booking channel determines which otherwise executable path preserves the complete user goal.
extension_candidates.wrong_action_consequence: The locally successful path irreversibly loses a required benefit or reservation identity.
extension_candidates.ordinary_retry: Potentially blocked after cancellation or benefit consumption.
extension_candidates.experience_identifiability: Needs both channel directions and matched goals.
extension_candidates.overlap: May blur capability with policy eligibility and requires more new state than EE-01.

extension_candidates.name: RETAIL_PATCH_REPLACE_CONTRACT
extension_candidates.native_anchor: Orders contain multi-item collections and item modification already commits a state transition.
extension_candidates.required_extension: Introduce versioned patch versus full-replacement payload semantics and a representation for unchanged items.
extension_candidates.latent_mapping: Observable API contract version determines payload construction.
extension_candidates.wrong_action_consequence: A partial payload under replacement semantics would silently drop omitted items.
extension_candidates.ordinary_retry: Could be blocked by the existing one-shot status transition.
extension_candidates.experience_identifiability: Would require paired versions and opposite payload cases.
extension_candidates.overlap: The current tool schema cannot express a clean reverse-direction case; full payloads can dominate patch payloads without additional concurrency semantics.

extension_candidates.name: RETAIL_ONE_SHOT_DISCLOSURE
extension_candidates.native_anchor: A partial successful item modification makes later item modification impossible.
extension_candidates.required_extension: None for state transition; User Simulator branching would be needed to hide a later requested change until the Agent elicits it.
extension_candidates.latent_mapping: The interaction strategy determines whether all desired changes are known before the one-shot write.
extension_candidates.wrong_action_consequence: Premature partial modification succeeds and makes the remaining requested modification unreachable.
extension_candidates.experience_identifiability: Could contrast vague confirmation with targeted completeness elicitation.
extension_candidates.overlap: The native policy already explicitly instructs the Agent to collect all changes, so this is more suitable for a later User Simulator primitive than the first hidden-environment primitive.

extension_candidates.name: POST_MUTATION_REVISION_REBINDING
extension_candidates.native_anchor: Native writes return committed state and stable reservation IDs.
extension_candidates.required_extension: Add replaceable segment/revision identifiers and a dependent segment-scoped write.
extension_candidates.latent_mapping: Mutation output or refreshed state determines the valid downstream binding.
extension_candidates.wrong_action_consequence: Using a retired binding fails or mutates the wrong target.
extension_candidates.ordinary_retry: A generic refresh may reveal and repair the target unless the design adds another commitment constraint.
extension_candidates.experience_identifiability: A refresh/rebind rule is learnable, but always refreshing remains safe on controls.
extension_candidates.overlap: This is the extension proposed after Primitive A failed; it still lacks a counter-directional Success case where unconditional refresh is harmful.

extension_candidates.name: SINGLE_USE_RESOURCE_LIFECYCLE
extension_candidates.latent_mapping: Certificate consumption should determine global allocation.
extension_candidates.wrong_action_consequence: Early redemption can make a later booking impossible.
extension_candidates.experience_identifiability: The rule is observable from failed reuse and missing certificate state.
extension_candidates.overlap: Completed HRS Core E0 was 12/12 because visible resource amounts revealed the correct allocation.

isolation_design.implementation_shape: A v3-owned DB extension plus AirlineTools subclass or composition, exposed through a separately registered process-local domain factory.
isolation_design.policy_rule: The one-change commitment limit is visible; only the channel-to-settlement mapping remains latent.
isolation_design.evaluation: Custom semantic evaluator checks final itinerary, payment delta, preserved fields, and consumed change budget without enforcing tool order.

recommendation.reason: It is the smallest audited option that can make the hidden mapping action-critical, make the wrong action succeed before delayed failure, block trial-and-error recovery, and reuse real native historical/current settlement structure.
remaining_risks: Overlap with v2 P2/P5 must be disclosed.
Channel naming or price geometry must not leak the mapping.
The change budget must be explicit rather than hidden.
Two counter-directional tasks must prove that no single fixed action dominates.
